Package org.spongepowered.gradle.plugin.config

Class GameTestConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.spongepowered.gradle.plugin.config.GameTestConfiguration
public abstract class GameTestConfiguration extends Object
Runs the plugin's gametests, the @GameTest methods under src/gametest, through the gametest test suite and its task, or another one, see getSuite(): the platform's gametest module is added to the suite's classpath, the Sponge runtime boots in its JVM before JUnit discovers anything, and the plugin's own output is handed to it to load. Unless gametests are put in test, it is left alone, so unit tests run without a game. Every value has a working default.

    • getRequired

      public org.gradle.api.provider.Property<Boolean> getRequired()
      Whether failing gametests fail the build, the default. The gametest task always runs as part of check; required(false) makes it an optional check, whose failures are reported without failing the build.

    • required

      public void required(boolean required)

    • getSuite

      public org.gradle.api.provider.Property<String> getSuite()
      The JVM test suite the gametests run in, with its source set and task of the same name; gametest by default. A suite of that name that exists already is used as it is, as test is with suite("test"), which runs the gametests in src/test through the test task alongside any unit tests. Otherwise the plugin creates it, on top of the plugin's own classes and dependencies, once sponge.gameTests is configured.

    • suite

      The version of the platform's gametest module, org.spongepowered:<platform>-gametest. Defaults to the version of the Sponge runtime runServer resolves, so the two always match.

    • getPluginFiles

      public org.gradle.api.file.ConfigurableFileCollection getPluginFiles()
      What Sponge loads as the plugin under test, as one plugin resource: by default the main and gametest outputs and the jars of the projects this one depends on, a multi-module plugin's other parts. A built jar can stand in, e.g. plugin(tasks.named("shadowJar")). Jars are listed before directories, since Sponge reads the manifest from the last path.

    • plugin

      public void plugin(Object... paths)

    • getLibraries

      public org.gradle.api.file.ConfigurableFileCollection getLibraries()
      What Sponge loads beside the plugin as game-layer libraries, each its own module. The modules on the gametest runtime classpath are there by default, less JUnit and anything the game loads itself: Minecraft and the API with their dependencies, and the libraries the Sponge runtime installs. libraries(...) adds to that: a file dependency, a configuration, a task's jar.
